# AI-PROVIDER OBLIGATIONS → iGrowFast WEBSITE / TERMS / PRIVACY

## 0. THREE CORRECTIONS TO WIDELY-REPEATED CLAIMS (verified against primary sources)

**(a) Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.** Secondary sources (incl. vendor-comparison sites) claim Anthropic "participates in the DPF." **False.** I queried the US Commerce Dept's authoritative DPF list backend directly (`POST https://dpfapi.azurewebsites.net/api/participants`, the endpoint behind https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list). Control queries resolve correctly (`Google` → "Google LLC", EUCert Active). Results: `Anthro*` → **0 records** across Active/Inactive/Withdrawn. `Open*` → 15 Active, resolved by name: OpenClinica, OpenEvidence, PC Open, OpenID Foundation, OPENLANE, Openprise, OpenSesame, Open Space Labs, OpenTable, OpenTech Alliance, Open Text, OpenX, FIS, Advanced Solutions, Learning Technologies — **no OpenAI entity**. → **Both rely on SCCs, not DPF adequacy.** Any privacy-policy sentence claiming DPF coverage would be false.

**(b) OpenAI's Usage Policies contain NO AI-disclosure requirement.** Many sources (and my own first search) assert OpenAI requires developers to "provide clear disclosure that AI is being used." The **current** policy (Effective **October 29, 2025**, retrieved in full) does **not**. The 2025-10-29 rewrite consolidated everything into a "universal set of policies" and dropped the old developer-specific disclosure duty. What remains relevant: prohibitions on "deceit, fraud, scams, spam, or impersonation" and "automation of high-stakes decisions in sensitive areas without human review" (list = critical infrastructure, education, housing, employment, financial/credit, insurance, legal, medical, essential government services, product safety, national security, migration, law enforcement — **COD e-commerce is not listed**). → **Anthropic is the stricter provider on disclosure; OpenAI's constraint is anti-deception, not affirmative disclosure.**
Source: https://openai.com/policies/usage-policies/

**(c) "Powered by GPT" is explicitly prohibited.** Older guidance about a "Powered by OpenAI badge" is stale plugin-era text. The current brand page lists **`GPT-powered`** verbatim as a **Don't**.

*(Note: openai.com is Cloudflare-blocked to automated fetchers (403 to both the fetch tool and curl). I retrieved the official OpenAI texts via Internet Archive raw snapshots of the openai.com originals — usage-policies snapshot 2026-07-11, brand 2026-07-11, DPA 2026-07-07, enterprise-privacy 2026-07-15, services-agreement 2026-06-01, policies index 2026-07-14. These are the official pages, archived, not third-party paraphrase.)*

---

## 1. ANTHROPIC — Commercial Terms + Usage Policy

**Usage Policy (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup) — the single hardest requirement in this whole report:**
> "All consumer-facing chatbots, including any external-facing or interactive AI agent, must disclose to users that they are interacting with AI rather than a human. This disclosure must be provided at a minimum at the beginning of each chat session."

It sits under **"Additional Use Case Guidelines"**, introduced by: *"The below use cases – regardless of whether they are High-Risk Use Cases – **must comply** with the additional guidance provided."* → **Mandatory, not advisory.** An AI-generated WhatsApp reply to a seller's end-customer is exactly "an external-facing or interactive AI agent." **This is a product change (a disclosure in the WhatsApp chat flow), not website text.**

Reinforcing prohibition (under "Do Not Compromise Privacy or Identity Rights"):
> "Impersonate a human by presenting results as human-generated, or using results in a manner intended to convince a natural person that they are communicating with a natural person when they are not"

**High-Risk Use Cases** (require human-in-the-loop + per-session disclosure): Legal, Healthcare, Insurance, Finance, Employment/housing, Academic testing, Media/journalistic content. **COD order confirmation is NOT high-risk** → the human-in-the-loop duty does not bite. Only the chatbot-disclosure rule does.

**Other AUP prohibitions that touch this product:**
- "Promote or facilitate the generation or distribution of spam"
- "Utilize automation in account creation or to engage in spammy behavior"
- **"Engage in actions or behaviors that circumvent the guardrails or terms of other platforms or services"** ← see §6, the WhatsApp-stack risk.

**Commercial Terms (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms):**
- **§B**: "Customer (a) retains all rights to its Inputs, and (b) owns its Outputs." and **"Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services."** → no training, contractually guaranteed, no config needed.
- **§C**: "Data submitted through the Services will be processed in accordance with the Anthropic Data Processing Addendum ('DPA'), **which is incorporated into these Terms by reference**." → **No DPA signature required.** (Confirmed: https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996862 — "automatically incorporated into our Commercial Terms of Service.")
- **§D.3 (Limitations of Outputs; Notice to Users)**: Customer "acknowledges, **and must notify its Users**, that factual assertions in Outputs should not be relied upon without independently checking their accuracy, as they may be false, incomplete, misleading or not reflective of recent events or information." → **an affirmative obligation that lands in iGrowFast's own ToS/UI.**
- **§D.4**: no competing product, no reselling the Services except as approved.
- **§G (Publicity)**: this clause lets **Anthropic** use *iGrowFast's* name/logo (opt-out available). It grants iGrowFast **nothing** in return.

**Retention (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention + https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866):**
- API inputs/outputs auto-deleted **within 30 days**.
- **Flagged by trust & safety → retained up to 2 years**; T&S classification scores **up to 7 years**.
- ZDR available per-organization **on request via sales** (contract + config, not self-serve).
- Note: **Claude Fable 5 / Mythos 5 are "Covered Models" requiring mandatory 30-day retention — ZDR unavailable for them.**

**Data residency (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/data-residency): `inference_geo` accepts only `"us"` or `"global"`; Workspace geo `"us"` only. There is NO EU residency option.** → US transfer is unavoidable with Anthropic.

**Anthropic DPA (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum, Effective Feb 24, 2025):**
- **§B.1: "With respect to Customer Personal Data, Customer is the controller and Anthropic is Customer's processor."**
- §A.8 / §I.1: SCC **"Module Two (controller to processor) and/or Module Three (processor to processor)"** incorporated by reference. **DPF not mentioned anywhere.**
- Subprocessors: https://www.anthropic.com/subprocessors, ~15-day objection window.
- Deletion within 30 days of termination.
- **⚠ STRUCTURAL MISMATCH:** §B.1 hard-codes **Customer = controller**. But for end-customer data (names, phones, addresses, order contents, WhatsApp content) belonging to sellers' customers, **iGrowFast is a processor, not a controller**. Anthropic's DPA does not contain language contemplating Customer acting as a processor for a third-party controller, even though Module Three is incorporated. **Contrast OpenAI, which handles this explicitly** (§8.1: *"Module Three (Processor to Sub-Processor) of the SCCs apply when Customer is a Data Processor and OpenAI is processing Customer Data as a sub-processor."*). → **Counsel item. OpenAI's paper is a better fit for processor-role data than Anthropic's.**

**Trademark:** Anthropic publishes **no third-party "Powered by Claude" badge programme** (no /legal/trademark-policy exists — 404). Consumer Terms state: *"You may not, without our prior written permission, use our name, logos, or other trademarks"* → contact **marketing@anthropic.com**. The Commercial Terms grant no trademark licence.

---

## 2. OPENAI

**Services Agreement (https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/) — governs business/API use:**
- **§4.2**: "OpenAI will only use Customer Content as necessary to provide Customer with the Services, comply with applicable law, enforce the OpenAI Policies, and prevent abuse. **OpenAI will not use Customer Content to develop or improve the Services, unless Customer explicitly agrees to such use.**" → no training by default.
- **§3.2 (End Users)** — *the key one for Q7*: "**Customer will obtain and maintain from End Users any consents necessary** to allow Administrators to engage in the activities described in the Agreement **and to allow OpenAI to deliver the Services**." → OpenAI contractually pushes the consent burden onto iGrowFast.
- §4.1: Customer retains Input ownership, owns Output (assigned).
- §4.3: "Customer is responsible for all Input and **represents and warrants that it has all rights, licenses, and permissions required to provide Input to the Services**." → sending sellers' end-customer PII/WhatsApp content is a warranty iGrowFast is making.
- §11.3: Customer Content deleted within 30 days of termination.
- §16.12: Supported Countries only.

**Data handling (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data + https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/):**
- "Data sent to the OpenAI API is not used to train or improve OpenAI models (unless you explicitly opt in)." (API since **March 1, 2023**.)
- Default: "OpenAI may securely retain API inputs and outputs for **up to 30 days**… After 30 days, API inputs and outputs are removed from our systems, unless we are legally required to retain them." Abuse-monitoring logs ≤30 days.
- **ZDR** requires **prior approval** (contact sales); eligible endpoints incl. `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/moderations`, `/v1/audio/*`. Under ZDR `store` is forced `false`.

**OpenAI DPA (https://openai.com/policies/data-processing-addendum/, Effective January 1, 2026):**
- **⚠ MUST BE EXECUTED — it is NOT auto-incorporated like Anthropic's.** The page carries a live execution link: **https://ironcladapp.com/public-launch/63ffefa2bed6885f4536d0fe** ("Execute Data Processing Agreement"). *(The preamble does say "By clicking 'I agree,' accepting the Order Form, or using the Services, Customer agrees" — but the presence of a dedicated execution link means the defensible path is to sign it. Treat as a signature action.)*
- **§4.1 EEA/Swiss**: Customer instructs **OpenAI Ireland Limited** to process EEA/Swiss data; onward transfers outside the EEA ride on "agreements containing **SCCs**… or an adequacy decision issued by the European Commission under Article 45 GDPR." **No DPF reliance.**
- **§8.1**: Module Two when Customer is controller; **Module Three when Customer is a Data Processor and OpenAI is a sub-processor** ← fits iGrowFast's processor role.
- §2.9: general authorization + 30-day objection; Sub-Processor List: **https://platform.openai.com/subprocessors**.
- §2.11: return/deletion on termination. §5.1: OpenAI does not "sell"/"share" (CCPA).
- SCCs = EU Commission clauses adopted **June 4, 2021**; UK Addendum applies to UK data.

---

## 3. BRANDING — precise rules (they differ sharply)

**OpenAI (https://openai.com/brand/):**
- **DO**: *"Pawtopia is building on OpenAI"*; *"Pawtopia product was developed on GPT-4"*
- **DON'T**: *"Pawtopia collaborated with OpenAI"* / *"worked with OpenAI"* / *"partnered with OpenAI"* / **"Pawtopia is building with OpenAI"** ← note "building **with**" is prohibited, "building **on**" is fine.
- **DON'T** (Models section): *"Use "GPT" generically without identifying the specific model: **GPT-powered**"* → **"Powered by GPT" is out.**
- *"We do not permit model names in app titles… **we do not permit our GPT brand to be used in app, product, developer or company names**."*
- *"everything about your app, product or company (including name, logo, description, slogan, tagline and screenshots) should be your own and should be free of OpenAI's brands… **You should not use the OpenAI logo or brand in any way that would imply sponsorship, affiliation or endorsement.**"*
- *"Do not feature our Marks more prominently than your own company's name or marks."* Permission is **non-exclusive, non-transferable, reviewable, and terminable at any time**.
- *"If you are an active OpenAI developer, you may **truthfully identify the OpenAI technology you use**."*
- **Content attribution**: *"If publishing text or images generated by an OpenAI model, **you are not required to attribute**."*
- Contact: legal@openai.com / partnercomms@openai.com.

**⚠ CONFLICT FOUND:** The **Sharing & publication policy** (https://openai.com/policies/sharing-publication-policy/, *"Updated: November 14, 2022"*) — **still listed on the live /policies index as of the 2026-07-14 snapshot, so still operative** — says for first-party content co-authored with the API: *"The published content is attributed to your name or company"* and *"The role of AI in formulating the content is **clearly disclosed in a way that no reader could possibly miss**."* This **contradicts** the newer brand page's "not required to attribute." → For AI-written **marketing copy on the website**, take the conservative path (disclose).

**Anthropic:** no badge programme; **"Powered by Claude" requires prior written permission** (marketing@anthropic.com). Safest permitted-by-default posture = a factual, non-logo statement.

**→ Recommended safe wording:** "iGrowFast is built on OpenAI and Anthropic technology." / "AI features built on Claude (Anthropic) and OpenAI models." **No logos. No "Powered by GPT." No "partnered/built with." Our name more prominent than theirs.**

---

## 4. EU AI ACT — ⚠ ARTICLE 50(1) BITES IN ~2 WEEKS (2 AUGUST 2026)

**Article 113 (verified against the regulation's own text):** *"It shall apply from 2 August 2026. However: (a) Chapters I and II shall apply from 2 February 2025; (b) Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII and Chapter XII and Article 78 shall apply from 2 August 2025…; (c) Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations… shall apply from 2 August 2027."* → **Chapter IV (Article 50) is NOT carved out → applies from 2 August 2026.**

**Digital Omnibus did NOT rescue this.** Adopted: EP plenary **16 June 2026** (423/57/174), Council final green light **29 June 2026**. What actually moved (per the EP's own Legislative Train + EP press release 20260611IPR45207):
- **High-risk** → **2 December 2027** (stand-alone) / **2 August 2028** (embedded in products). *Delayed.*
- **Marking/watermarking of AI-generated content (Art 50(2))** → **2 December 2026** for systems placed on the market before 2 Aug 2026. *Delayed.*
- **Art 50(1) chatbot disclosure → NOT delayed. Still 2 August 2026.**

**Art 50(1):** *"Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, **unless this is obvious** from the point of view of a natural person who is reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect…"*
**Art 50(5):** *"…provided to the natural persons concerned in a **clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure**."*

**Who is iGrowFast?** Art 3(1) *provider* = *"…develops an AI system… and places it on the market or **puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark**, whether for payment or free of charge."* iGrowFast builds an AI messaging feature into its own SaaS and offers it under the iGrowFast name → **iGrowFast is the PROVIDER of that AI system** (Anthropic/OpenAI are providers of the underlying GPAI models). So **Art 50(1) binds iGrowFast directly**, not just the deployer duties. iGrowFast is also a *deployer* (Art 3(4)).

**Does it apply at all? — the honest scoping answer.** Art 2(1): (a) providers placing on the EU market *"irrespective of whether those providers are established… within the Union or in a third country"*; (b) deployers established in the Union; **(c) "providers and deployers of AI systems that have their place of establishment or are located in a third country, where the output produced by the AI system is used in the Union."**
→ A Wyoming LLC with Morocco-centric users is **outside scope today** if no AI output is used in the Union. **But**: the stated positioning is "worldwide," and **one EU-based seller — or one AI-generated WhatsApp message read by an end-customer in the EU — triggers Art 2(1)(c)**. The German Contabo VPS does **not** by itself trigger the AI Act (Art 2 keys on market/output, not infrastructure). **Given "worldwide" marketing, build the disclosure now — Anthropic's AUP mandates it globally anyway (§1), so this costs nothing extra.**

**The "obvious" exception does NOT save you:** a WhatsApp reply that appears to come from the seller's own store number is precisely the case where AI involvement is *not* obvious.

---

## 5. GDPR + MOROCCO — the transfer analysis (Q3, Q7)

**GDPR territorial scope — likely NOT triggered, but flag for counsel.** Art 3(1) requires processing "in the context of the activities of **an establishment**" in the Union. Settled CJEU doctrine (*Weltimmo* C-230/14) treats "establishment" as requiring effective and real exercise of activity through stable arrangements — **renting VPSs from Contabo in Germany is infrastructure, not an establishment**. Art 3(2) turns on **targeting**: offering goods/services to data subjects in the Union, or monitoring their behaviour. Morocco-centric operations with a French-language UI aimed at Moroccan sellers → **GDPR probably does not apply merely because the servers sit in Germany.** ⚠ *Caveat: I could not extract EDPB Guidelines 3/2018 (the PDF fetch failed), so I am asserting this from the Regulation's text + established CJEU doctrine rather than from a verbatim EDPB quote. Confirm with counsel before relying on it; do not put a "GDPR does not apply to us" claim on the website.*

**⚠⚠ MOROCCO LAW 09-08 / CNDP IS THE ACTUALLY-BINDING REGIME — AND IT BLOCKS US TRANSFERS.**
This is the biggest operational finding in the report and it is **not** a website-text item.

**CNDP Délibération n°236-2015 (18 Dec 2015)** — modifying n°465-2013 — establishes the list of states offering sufficient protection. I extracted the official PDF text verbatim (https://www.cndp.ma/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/deliberation-n-236-2015-18-12-2015.pdf). **Article 1**, full list:
> *"Allemagne, Autriche, Belgique, Bulgarie, Canada, Chypre, Danemark, Espagne, Estonie, Finlande, France, Grèce, Hongrie, Irlande, Islande, Italie, Lettonie, Liechtenstein, Lituanie, Luxembourg, Malte, Norvège, Pays-Bas, Pologne, Portugal, République Tchèque, Roumanie, Royaume-Uni, Slovaquie, Slovénie, Suède, Suisse."*

→ **The United States is NOT on the list.** (Germany **is** → the Contabo VPS and the EU-hosted messaging provider are fine.) Article 2: *"Tout amendement de la liste susmentionnée fera l'objet d'une nouvelle délibération"* — I found no later deliberation amending it; the 2015 list is still operative.

**Consequence:** Sending Moroccan end-customers' names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, order contents and **WhatsApp message content** to Anthropic or OpenAI (both US, and Anthropic has **no** EU residency option) is a **transfer to a non-adequate country under Law 09-08 Art. 43–44**. It requires **either**:
- **express prior CNDP authorization** — *"Sur autorisation expresse de la CNDP si le traitement garantit un niveau de protection suffisant"* — via **Form F118**, CNDP opinion within **2 months**, and critically *"l'autorisation de transfert à l'étranger d'un fichier de données personnelles n'est accordée que lorsque le traitement sous-jacent a fait l'objet d'une demande de déclaration ou d'autorisation approuvée par la CNDP"* (**the underlying processing must already be declared/approved first** — so this is a two-step filing chain with lead time); **or**
- **an Art. 44 exception**, most plausibly the data subject's **explicit consent** to the transfer, or necessity for contract performance.
Sources: https://www.cndp.ma/transfert-de-donnees-a-letranger/ , https://www.cndp.ma/notifier-une-demande-de-transfert-a-letranger/
Sanctions for non-compliance are reported at up to 1 year imprisonment + MAD 200,000 (secondary sources; verify the exact Law 09-08 penal articles with Moroccan counsel).

**Legal basis / role analysis (Q7).** For end-customer data, **iGrowFast is a processor and the seller is the controller.** Therefore:
- **iGrowFast cannot self-authorise sending that data to an AI provider.** It needs the seller-controller's **documented instruction + sub-processor authorisation** (GDPR Art 28(2)/(4) logic, and the equivalent under 09-08). Adding Anthropic/OpenAI as sub-processors without the sellers' authorisation is the classic failure mode here.
- The **legal basis sits with the seller** (contract performance for order handling; consent where required). iGrowFast's job is to (i) get the authorisation in its seller DPA, (ii) name the AI sub-processors to sellers, (iii) give sellers an objection right, (iv) supply the notice text sellers must show *their* customers.
- For **iGrowFast's own users** (sellers, media buyers, couriers) iGrowFast is a **controller** → its own privacy policy + legal basis apply directly.

**Generic processor category — is it sufficient? (explicit answer to your constraint.)**
- **On the public website/privacy policy: YES.** GDPR Art 13(1)(e)/14(1)(e) require *"the recipients **or categories of recipients**"* — categories are expressly permitted. **"Messaging infrastructure providers, EU-hosted" is defensible as public notice text.** (Same logic under 09-08's information duty.)
- **In the seller DPA: NO.** Sub-processors must be **named** so the controller can exercise the objection right. A category is not enough there.
- **In the CNDP F118 filing: NO.** The filing must identify the actual recipient, country, and safeguards.
- **Same rule applies to the AI providers**: you may write "AI service providers (United States)" as a *category* on the website, but Anthropic and OpenAI must be **named** in the seller DPA and in the CNDP filing.

---

## 6. ⚠ THE WHATSAPP-STACK RISK (flagging honestly — you asked me to report carefully)

Anthropic's AUP prohibits: *"**Engage in actions or behaviors that circumvent the guardrails or terms of other platforms or services**."* The product's messaging today runs through third-party messaging infrastructure. **If that stack is an unofficial WhatsApp automation layer (i.e. not WhatsApp Business Platform/Cloud API), then using Claude to generate messages that are delivered through it is arguably facilitating circumvention of Meta's terms — an AUP violation independent of anything on the website.** OpenAI's equivalent hook is §3.3(b) *"use the Services or Customer Content in a way that violates third parties' rights"* and the Usage Policy's "deceit… spam… impersonation."
This is an **architecture/vendor decision, not website text**, and I flag it because you asked specifically about restrictions on generating messages sent to consumers via WhatsApp. **Neither Usage Policy names WhatsApp; neither prohibits AI-generated consumer messaging as such.** The exposure is (i) the circumvention clause above, (ii) the spam prohibitions, and (iii) the impersonation prohibition — which the AI-disclosure requirement (§1) directly cures. Migrating to the official WhatsApp Business Platform removes (i) entirely.

- **COD e-commerce is not a "high-risk use case"** under either policy → no human-in-the-loop mandate, and EU AI Act high-risk (now 2027/2028) does not reach it.
- Anthropic's DPA needs **no signature**.

# 4. THE TOP 10 THINGS THAT WILL ACTUALLY BACKFIRE

Ranked by **probability × severity × irreversibility**. Blunt.

### 1. Netting commission out of collected COD — or shipping a "wallet"
**Loi 103-12 Art 183: 6 months–3 years imprisonment + 100,000–5,000,000 MAD.** The instant COD proceeds hit an iGrowFast account, or commission is netted from collected cash, or a seller can draw down an on-platform balance, you are an **unlicensed établissement de paiement** performing *"opérations de transfert de fonds"* as *"intermédiaire entre le payeur et le fournisseur de biens et services"*, *à titre de profession habituelle*. **And iGrowFast LLC structurally cannot cure it**: Art 35-2 requires a **société anonyme or SARL** — Moroccan forms. A Wyoming LLC is neither. The cure is a Moroccan subsidiary + BAM capital + business plan + BAM review = **12–24 months, capital-intensive.** Note the severity gap: **3 years vs. 1 year, 5M MAD vs. 400k — this is an order of magnitude worse than the entire data-protection schedule combined.** And **Art 182 makes the marketing copy itself the offence** (3 mo–1 yr + 20k–200k) — a "wallet" UI or "we pay your sellers" headline is punishable **before a single dirham moves**. Free to comply with today. Catastrophic and unfixable if breached. **This is the item to get right before anything else on this page.**

### 2. The US leg of your own architecture is already illegal in Morocco, and no page fixes it
The **USA is absent** from the CNDP adequacy list (Délibération 236-2015 — Germany is on it; the US is not). **iGrowFast LLC's own US-based admin/support access to Moroccan personal data is itself a transfer to a non-adequate state.** Read that again: **the company's American nationality creates the violation.** Being a US entity is a **liability** here, not a shield. Add Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, TikTok, Snap, GA, Meta Ads, Shopify. **No Art 44 derogation is available at scale** — express consent is impossible (the sellers' customers never interact with you), and Art 44-1(d) contract-necessity collapses for AI and ad platforms because those are not *necessary* to execute the sale. Only **Art 44-3** (express, reasoned CNDP authorization) covers it, it is **not self-executing** (SCCs are not an instrument in Morocco), it takes 2 months, and it **presupposes an approved déclaration that does not exist**. **Price this correctly: the fines are not the risk.** Art 60 → 400k MAD (~USD 40k) is noise. The risks are **(i) personal criminal liability of directors** (Art 64 — *"sans préjudice des peines qui peuvent être appliquées à ses dirigeants"*), **(ii) a court order to erase the production database** (Art 61), **(iii) CNDP's public naming register** (live since 31 Mar 2023 — see the **TLSCONTACT** precedent: hearing 6 Jan 2023, compliance deadline 28 Feb 2023, Arts 52 and 60 invoked, referral to competent authorities), and **(iv) contamination of your seller base** — who are the Art 2-2(a) controllers with **Moroccan assets to seize**. A CNDP enforcement wave against sellers makes iGrowFast the reason their clients got fined. That kills the company commercially long before any criminal process concludes.

### 3. Launching the marketing site with ad pixels and no consent gate
**You are currently out of GDPR scope for the thing that actually matters** — Moroccan end-customers are not in the Union, so their names, phones, addresses and order contents are outside GDPR **no matter where you host them** (nationality is irrelevant; **location at the moment of the trigger activity** is what counts). And renting Contabo VPSs does **not** create an establishment — the Directive 95/46 "use of equipment" criterion was **deliberately deleted** from the GDPR, and EDPB Example 7 is your fact pattern. **Then you put a Meta Pixel on the homepage and hand it all away.** Art 3(2)(b) monitoring has **no intent requirement** (unlike 3(2)(a)); retargeting on an EU-reachable site *is* monitoring. That single tag triggers: Art 27 EU rep, a **separate** UK rep, the full Art 13 stack — **and Guidelines 05/2021 fn.15 makes YOU the exporter** (*"personal data disclosed via cookies are… a transmission by the operator of the website"* — you cannot hide behind "the user's browser sent it"). **Multiplied by: no establishment = no one-stop-shop under GDPR, and the OSS never applies to ePrivacy at all.** You face **27 supervisory authorities individually, with no lead-authority shield, and no way to buy one** without an EU establishment that would itself trigger Art 3(1) for everything. This is entirely self-inflicted, entirely preventable, and costs one configuration decision.

### 4. TCPA
**$500 per message, trebled to $1,500 for willful/knowing, per message, no statutory cap, private right of action, the most-classed statute in the US.** 100,000 non-compliant messages = **$50M–$150M nominal**. "Willful" under the Communications Act means **a conscious act, irrespective of intent to violate** — a low bar. The WhatsApp-is-not-a-"call" argument is **probably right and completely unadjudicated**: *"treat this as an argument you would win, not a rule you can build a business on."* Any **SMS fallback, OTP, or carrier-network message is squarely in scope**. **The indemnity is worthless** — it is paperwork from a judgment-proof Moroccan micro-seller, and under the FCC's 2013 *DISH Network* ruling a platform that supplies templates, schedules sends, optimizes timing, or auto-triggers messages on order events **looks like the "maker/initiator"** and is liable **directly**, plus **vicariously** under agency (actual authority, apparent authority, ratification). **The engineering controls are the defense.** And the **cross-subject-matter revocation prong went live 11 April 2026**: an opt-out on a **delivery notification** must now kill **marketing**. Also live: state **mini-TCPAs** (FL, OK, MD, WA CEMA, NJ), several drafted around **"text message"** rather than "call" — which **routes around *Steidinger* entirely**. And do not over-read *Steidinger v. Blackstone* (7th Cir., 14 Jul 2026): it kills the **§227(c)(5)** DNC private action for texts **only**; **§227(b)** — where the class-action money is — is untouched, and *Howard v. RNC* (9th Cir., 13 Jan 2026) went the other way. **Live circuit split.** Separately, the **highest-probability** Moroccan trigger in the whole stack sits adjacent: WhatsApp broadcast = **prospection directe** (Art 59) — *"recipients notice it directly."*

### 5. Shipping AI features over customer / WhatsApp content
Four regimes fire simultaneously. **Morocco Art 12-1(b)**: sending order data and message content to Anthropic/OpenAI is *"l'utilisation de données à caractère personnel à d'autres fins que celles pour lesquelles elles ont été collectées"* → **AUTORISATION (F112, 2 months), not a déclaration** — *"the single most under-appreciated trigger in the stack"* — plus **Art 54 criminal exposure** (3 mo–1 yr + 20k–200k, doubled). **Shopify PPA**: absolute ban on using Merchant/Customer Data — *"or enabling third parties to use"* it — to train, fine-tune or improve any ML/AI system. **Meta Platform Terms**: solely for clients' purposes, **segregated**, no cross-client features. **GDPR Art 28(10)**: *"if a processor infringes this Regulation by determining the purposes and means of processing, the processor shall be considered to be a controller"* → you have breached the DPA **and you have no legal basis**. Stacked on top: **Anthropic's DPA hard-codes you as controller** when you are a processor, and **AI Act Art 50(1) disclosure binds from 2 August 2026** — **not delayed by the Digital Omnibus**, whatever the delay headlines said. And **message content will incidentally contain health, religious and political data** — *"a COD platform processing raw message bodies cannot credibly assert it never touches sensitive data"* (Art 12-1(a)), on which **there is no Moroccan doctrine at all** (UNCERTAIN).

### 6. Publishing a retention schedule or a rights portal you haven't built
**Both CPPA orders were mechanism failures, not policy-text failures.** **Todd Snyder — $345,178**: a misconfigured privacy portal silently dropped opt-outs **for 40 days**. **Honda — $632,500**: verification demanded before an opt-out, asymmetric choices, agent friction. **Nomi**: promised an in-store opt-out that never existed — the FTC did not allege Nomi lied about *what* it collected; **it lied about a control it offered.** *"A 'Do Not Sell' link that doesn't work is worse than no link."* The same logic destroys a retention table that your **backups, your R2 media store, your blind-HMAC keyword index, and your AI vendors' logs** quietly contradict — that is simultaneously a **§5 deception** and an **Art 5(2) accountability failure**, and WP260 sets the bar at *"phrased in a way that allows the data subject to assess, on the basis of his or her own situation, what the retention period will be."* **Your `/privacy#retention` table is the single sentence on this website most likely to be false on the day it ships.** Ship the deletion jobs first, then the table.

### 7. Any US-hosting implication, on a site whose servers are in Germany
**The entire marketing positioning is "a US company."** That makes the US-hosting implication **the highest-probability §5 trap for this specific company** — a reader's default inference, not a claim you have to make. And it is false: VPSs are in **Germany (Contabo)**; the messaging vendor is **EU-hosted**. The precedent is exact and expensive: **GoodRx $1.5M**, **BetterHelp $7.8M**, **Avast $16.5M** (banned from selling browsing data; **$15.3M paid to 103,152 consumers in Dec 2025**) — all policies that **misdescribed data flows and third parties**. Adjacent and equally cheap to prove: calling **30 N Gould St Ste R** — *"one of the most heavily-used mass registered-agent addresses in the US"* — "our headquarters", or claiming a "US-based team/support" that does not exist. **A competitor or a journalist proves that in one search.** And understand the real penalty: **§5 alone carries no first-violation fine** (and after *AMG Capital* (2021) the FTC cannot get equitable monetary relief under §13(b)) — the punishment is an **injunction, a 20-year consent order, deletion and algorithmic disgorgement, and reputational kill.** The 20-year order is the sentence. Fix: **state the German hosting plainly.** *"The mismatch is only damaging when it looks concealed."*

### 8. A WhatsApp logo, a UI clone, or an "Official Partner" badge — on the page the Meta reviewer opens while deciding
**Business Verification is a hard gate before App Review**, and the **website is itself a submitted verification field**. So the reviewer reads your marketing site while deciding whether to trust you. On it, pre-approval, they find: a partner badge you never earned, the WhatsApp glyph you have no licence to display (*"the guidelines don't grant third parties a general marketing licence to display the logo"* — the nominative carve-out **explicitly withholds it**), and a pixel-faithful WhatsApp-chrome clone in `#25D366`. That is **the exact "conveys a relationship that doesn't exist" pattern**, on the exact page, at the exact moment. Compounding it: **"built on the WhatsApp Business Platform" / "official Cloud API"** is **false today** because messaging runs through a third-party provider — *"a reviewer who sees an unapproved applicant already claiming official-API status reads it as either misrepresentation or evidence of unofficial-access use — the latter being an independent basis for denial."* And **it costs you nothing commercially to avoid**: build the demo in your own design language — which is what you're actually selling — and say "Works with WhatsApp" in text. *"This is the claim most likely to appear on a founder-written landing page — kill it now."* Separately, the same third-party stack is arguably an **Anthropic AUP breach today** (*"circumvent the guardrails or terms of other platforms"*) regardless of what the website says.

### 9. Subscription billing without the ROSCA stack
**Click-to-cancel (16 CFR Part 425) was VACATED IN ITS ENTIRETY by the Eighth Circuit on 8 July 2025 — six days before its compliance date. It never took effect.** Do not read that as safety. The grounds were **procedural** (the FTC skipped the preliminary regulatory analysis after its own ALJ found >$100M impact); **the substantive policy was not repudiated**, and an **ANPRM went to OIRA on 30 January 2026**. Meanwhile **ROSCA (15 U.S.C. §8403) is fully in force** and is the live vehicle: **Amazon — $2.5B** (25 Sep 2025; $1B civil penalty + $1.5B redress to ~35M consumers; **two named executives, an SVP and a VP, personally charged**); **Chegg — $7.5M**; **FTC v. Uber** pending. **All three post-date or bracket the vacatur.** A ROSCA violation is treated as an **FTC rule violation → $53,088 per violation + redress + injunction.** Then **California's ARL** (AB 2863, contracts entered/amended/extended on or after 1 July 2025) adds a remedy that should stop the room: **non-compliant goods are deemed an unconditional gift — full refund of everything ever charged.** And note what Amazon means for the founder-anonymity constraint: **personal liability survives website anonymity.**

### 10. "Worldwide" + OFAC — and a sanctions clause copied from a template
iGrowFast LLC is a **US person**. OFAC prohibitions attach **wherever located**, and **liability is STRICT** — *"'We didn't know the user was in Iran' is not a defense."* **IEEPA: greater of ~$377,700 per violation or twice the transaction value; criminal up to $1,000,000 and 20 years.** Morocco is clean; **the "worldwide" pitch is what creates the surface** — and it is an adjective, not a strategy. Then the template betrays you: **every ToS on the internet still lists Syria, and that is now affirmatively wrong.** **E.O. 14312** (30 Jun 2025, effective 1 Jul 2025) terminated the national emergency and revoked E.O.s 13338/13399/13460/13572/13573/13582; the **Syrian Sanctions Regulations, 31 CFR Part 542, were REMOVED from the CFR on 26 August 2025.** Publishing a stale embargo list is a false term in your own contract. Equally wrong in the other direction: describing **Russia, Belarus or Venezuela as embargoed** — they are **targeted/sectoral, not territorial**. Correct list: **Cuba, Iran, North Korea + Crimea/DNR/LNR (+Kherson, Zaporizhzhia)**. **Reference the SDN List, not a hand-maintained country list that goes stale.** And the clause is worthless without **T1.9**: screening at signup, periodic re-screening, the **50 Percent Rule**, and a **log** — *"the record is what mitigates the penalty."*

**Honourable mentions that did not make the ten but will still hurt:** Morocco **Art 59 prospection directe** (highest *complaint* probability of anything here); **ADA/Unruh** ($4,000/violation + fees, plaintiff-chosen forum — Wyoming's 10th Circuit does not protect you); the **accessiBe overlay trap** ($1M — never repeat a vendor's compliance claim); **Meta's missing UK DPF extension**; **Shopify PPA §9.14** vs. the core loop; **Woo §1.2.9** vs. commission pricing; **CIN capture** silently escalating every filing.

## SEQUENCING — the only order that works

1. **T0.1** money-flow invariants (free, today, existential, gates everything commercial)
2. **T0.2** CNDP F211 déclaration → **récépissé in 24h** → unblocks `/privacy` §22, `/legal`, T0.3, T0.5
3. **T1.1** pixel/geo-gate decision → determines whether T1.12/T1.13 (EU + UK reps) are needed **before** `/privacy` can be finalised
4. **T2.1** Meta Business Verification (**longest wall-clock**, hard gate before App Review — start in parallel with 1–3)
5. **T0.3 / T0.4 / T0.5** CNDP F118 (Germany) → F118 (USA, Art 44-3) → F112 (AI) — **2 months each, sequential on T0.2**
6. Footer contract (§1.1) → `/legal` → `/privacy` → `/terms` → `/dpa` → `/acceptable-use` → `/cookies` → `/data-deletion` (**only after T1.4 backend**) → `/refunds` → `/accessibility` → `/`, `/about`, `/pricing`, `/integrations`, `/contact`
7. **T1.5** deletion jobs **before** the retention table publishes
8. **T2.10** crawler test from a US IP with a bot UA — **before** any platform submission

**The four things that gate the most downstream work:** the money-flow decision (T0.1), the CNDP déclaration (T0.2), the pixel decision (T1.1), and Meta verification (T2.1). Three of the four are free. None of them is a page.
